steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned slightly out.
Push your hips back and bend as if you were sitting down.
Knees track over your toes, back stays long, chest up.
Lower until your thighs are roughly horizontal, then drive powerfully back up.
squat.tip: Keep your weight across the whole sole, heels stay on the floor. 3×10–15 reps.
squat.caution: With knee or hip pain, only go as deep as you can without pain.
squat.progression: More reps, then weight (dumbbell/kettlebell), later pause squats.

steps: From standing, take a big step forward.
Bend both knees to ~90°, your back knee sinks towards the floor.
Front knee stays above the ankle, upper body upright.
Push back to standing through your front heel, then switch sides.
lunge.tip: Ideal for runners to tackle one-sided weaknesses. 3×8–10 each side.
lunge.caution: With knee problems, take shorter steps and don’t push your front knee past your toes.
lunge.progression: With weight, backwards or on the move (walking lunges).

steps: Hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, your body forms a straight line.
Brace your core firmly (no sagging hips).
Bend your elbows backwards and lower your chest towards the floor.
Push powerfully back up.
pushup.tip: Too hard? Drop to your knees or raise your hands (table/wall). 3×6–12.
pushup.caution: With shoulder or wrist trouble, do them raised against a bench or on your fists.
pushup.progression: From the wall to the bench, then to knees and full push-ups; later with your feet raised.

steps: Stand hip-width apart, weight in front of your shins.
Push your hips back, bend your knees only slightly, back stays straight.
Keep the weight close to your body, down to just below your knees.
Stand up by driving through your hips, squeeze your glutes.
deadlift.tip: The movement comes from your hips, not your back. Technique first, then weight. 3×8.
deadlift.caution: Keep your back neutral – skip it with acute back pain and get it checked.
deadlift.progression: More weight in small steps, then single-leg.

steps: Hip hinge as in the deadlift, upper body tilted forward ~45°.
Arms hang long, shoulder blades relaxed.
Pull the weight to your lower ribs, elbows close to your body.
Lower with control, your back stays stable.
row.tip: Balances out the front of the body that running favours. 3×10–12.
row.caution: Keep your back straight, don’t yank the weight.
row.progression: Heavier dumbbell or stronger band, lower slowly (3 s).

steps: Stand tall, weights at shoulder height.
Brace your core, don’t let your ribs flare.
Press the weights straight overhead until your arms are almost straight.
Lower with control back to shoulder height.
overhead_press.tip: No arched lower back – keep your abs tight. 3×8–10.
overhead_press.caution: With shoulder pain, don’t press overhead – sit down with a lighter weight instead, or skip it.
overhead_press.progression: More weight or one arm at a time (more core).

steps: Stand tall, if you like with the balls of your feet on a step.
Slowly rise onto your toes, hold briefly.
Lower with control, all the way down (on a step, below step height).
calf_raise.tip: Helps prevent Achilles and calf problems. 3×15–20, progress to single-leg if you like.
calf_raise.caution: With an irritated Achilles tendon, go slowly and don’t bounce.
calf_raise.progression: Single-leg, then on a step lowering below step level, then with weight.

steps: Forearms on the floor shoulder-width apart, elbows under your shoulders.
Your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Tighten your abs and glutes, tuck your pelvis slightly.
Keep breathing calmly, hold the position.
plank.tip: Better short and clean than long and sagging. 3×20–45 s.
plank.caution: No arched lower back – with back pain, start on your knees.
plank.progression: Hold longer, then lift an arm or a leg.

steps: Lie on your side, forearm under your shoulder, legs stacked.
Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line.
Reach your top arm to the ceiling or rest it on your hip.
Hold, then switch sides.
side_plank.tip: Stabilises your hips when you run. 3×15–30 s each side.
side_plank.caution: With shoulder trouble, support yourself on your knee.
side_plank.progression: Lift your top leg or raise and lower your hips.

steps: Lie on your back, feet flat and hip-width apart, arms by your sides.
Squeeze your glutes and push your hips up.
Thighs and torso form a line, hold briefly.
Lower with control without touching all the way down.
glute_bridge.tip: Wakes up the often “sleepy” glutes. 3×12–15, single-leg if you like.
glute_bridge.caution: Don’t push into an arched lower back – the power comes from your glutes.
glute_bridge.progression: Single-leg, then feet raised or with weight on your hips.

steps: Lie on your back, arms to the ceiling, hips and knees raised to 90°.
Gently press your lower back into the floor (abs tight).
Extend your right leg and left arm at the same time, without arching your back.
Back to the centre, then the other side.
dead_bug.tip: Core stability without loading the spine. 3×8 each side, slowly.
dead_bug.caution: Your lower back stays on the floor – otherwise make the movement smaller.
dead_bug.progression: Slower, arms/legs straight, later with a light weight.

steps: Stand tall and stable, abs tight.
Bend your upper body to the side with control, sliding your hand along your thigh.
Come back up using your side abs.
side_crunch.caution: Only bend to the side, don’t lean forward or twist.
side_crunch.progression: With a dumbbell in the hand on the opposite side.

steps: Deep lunge, back knee on the floor (e.g. on a cushion).
Tuck your pelvis slightly, squeeze your glutes.
Gently push your hips forward until you feel a stretch at the front of your hip.
Hold still, don’t bounce.
hip_flexor_stretch.tip: Important if you sit a lot and run. 2×30 s each side.
hip_flexor_stretch.caution: Pad your knee well; don’t compensate by arching your lower back.
hip_flexor_stretch.progression: Reach the arm on the back-leg side overhead.

steps: Place one leg slightly forward, heel on the floor, toes up.
Push your hips back and lean forward with a straight back.
Reach your hands towards your shin until you feel a light stretch at the back.
Hold, then switch sides.
hamstring_stretch.tip: Keep your back long – don’t round it. 2×30 s each side.
hamstring_stretch.caution: Only a light stretch – never jerky and not with a fresh strain.
hamstring_stretch.progression: Hold longer, consciously keeping your back long.

steps: Lean against the wall with both hands.
Extend one leg straight back, heel stays on the floor.
Push your hips forward until you feel it in your calf.
For the deep calf, bend your back knee slightly.
calf_stretch.tip: Feels good after a run. 2×30 s each side.
calf_stretch.caution: With an irritated Achilles tendon, stretch gently and not into pain.
calf_stretch.progression: Also with a bent knee (deep calf muscles).

steps: On all fours, hands under your shoulders, knees under your hips.
Inhale: let your back gently sag, look up (“cow”).
Exhale: round your back, chin to chest (“cat”).
Flow between the two several times in time with your breath.
cat_cow.tip: Gentle mobilisation for back and neck. 8–10 calm rounds.

steps: Stand tall, abs lightly engaged.
Open your arms backwards, loosely clasp your hands behind your back.
Lift your breastbone, shoulders back and down.
Breathe calmly, hold gently.
chest_opener.caution: With shoulder instability, don’t pull into the end position.
chest_opener.progression: Hold longer, arms a little higher.

steps: One foot forward on the floor, the top of your back foot rests on a chair or bench.
Upper body upright, bend your front knee and lower your body straight down.
Front knee stays over your foot, back knee sinks towards the floor.
Push up with control through your front heel.
split_squat.tip: Very effective for single-leg strength and stability. 3×8–10 each side.
split_squat.caution: With knee problems, don’t go as deep.
split_squat.progression: Bulgarian split squat (back foot raised), then with weight.

steps: Stand with your back flat against the wall, feet about 40 cm in front of it.
Slide down the wall until your thighs are horizontal.
Knees above your ankles, back stays against the wall.
Hold the position, breathing calmly.
wall_sit.tip: Static strength endurance for your legs – ideal without equipment. 3×30–45 s.
wall_sit.caution: With kneecap trouble, sit higher (angle above 90°).

steps: Stand in front of a sturdy, knee-high step.
Step all the way up with one foot, driving through the heel.
Stand steady at the top for a moment, then lower back down with control.
Don’t push off with your back leg – your top leg does the work.
step_up.tip: Runner-friendly (single-leg, close to everyday movement). 3×10 each side.
step_up.caution: Keep your knee stable – don’t let it cave inwards.

steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet hip-width apart on the floor.
Hands loosely at your temples (don’t pull on your head).
Curl your upper body up using your abs, shoulder blades lift slightly.
Hold briefly, lower slowly.
crunch.tip: The movement comes from your abs, not your neck. 3×12–20.
crunch.caution: Don’t pull on your neck with your hands.
crunch.progression: Slower, then with a light weight on your chest.

steps: Lie on your back, legs straight, hands beside or under your bottom.
Consciously keep your lower back on the floor.
Slowly raise your straight legs to ~90°.
Lower with control without fully resting your heels on the floor.
leg_raise.tip: If your back twinges, bend your knees slightly. 3×10–15.
leg_raise.caution: With back pain, keep your knees bent.

steps: Lie on your back, arms overhead, legs straight.
Press your lower back firmly into the floor (brace your abs).
Lift your shoulders and legs slightly – your body becomes a shallow bowl.
Keep breathing calmly and hold.
hollow_hold.tip: Your lower back must NOT lift off the floor. 3×15–30 s.
hollow_hold.caution: Your lower back mustn’t lift – if it does, pull your knees in.

steps: Lie face down, arms stretched out in front.
Lift your arms, chest and legs slightly off the floor at the same time.
Look at the floor, neck long – don’t crank your head back.
Hold briefly, lower gently.
superman.tip: Strengthens the often neglected posterior chain. 3×10 or hold 3×20 s.
superman.caution: The face-down extension puts more load on the lumbar spine – with back trouble, do the bird dog instead.
superman.progression: Hold longer, alternate arm and leg.

steps: On all fours, hands under your shoulders, knees under your hips.
Extend your right arm and left leg long at the same time.
Hips and shoulders stay level (no twisting).
Bring them back and switch sides.
bird_dog.tip: Stability, not momentum – slow and controlled. 3×8–10 each side.
bird_dog.caution: Keep your pelvis level, don’t arch your lower back.
bird_dog.progression: Hold briefly, then bring elbow and knee together under your body.

steps: From kneeling, sit your bottom back towards your heels.
Lower your upper body forward, stretch your arms long in front of you.
Forehead rests on the floor, shoulders relaxed.
Breathe deeply into your lower back.
child_pose.tip: Gentle relief for your whole back. 3×30–45 s.
child_pose.caution: With knee trouble, put a cushion between your bottom and your heels.
child_pose.progression: Walk your hands to the side (side stretch).

steps: Lie on your back, arms spread out to the sides (T shape).
Bend both knees and lower them together to one side.
Optionally turn your head the other way, keep both shoulders on the floor.
Breathe calmly, then switch sides.
supine_twist.tip: Loosens your lower back after a run. 2×30 s each side.
supine_twist.caution: Shoulders stay on the floor, don’t force it.
supine_twist.progression: Hold longer, straighten your top leg.

steps: Lie on your back, both knees bent.
Cross one ankle over the other knee (in the shape of a “4”).
Pull the lower leg towards your chest until you feel it in your glutes.
Hold, then switch sides.
figure_four.tip: A classic for tight glutes or a sciatica-like feeling in runners. 2×30 s each side.
figure_four.caution: With hip or knee pain, don’t pull as far.
figure_four.progression: Sitting on a chair, leaning forward.

steps: Sit tall, bring the soles of your feet together in front of you.
Draw your heels in loosely, let your knees sink to the sides.
Stay upright, lean your upper body slightly forward.
Don’t bounce – hold still.
butterfly_stretch.tip: Opens up your hips and inner thighs. 2×30–45 s.
butterfly_stretch.caution: Don’t press on your knees or bounce.

steps: Part 1 (approx. 8 min): easy running with hip out/in, sideways shuffle, shoulder contact with a partner, short bursts forwards and backwards.
Part 2 (approx. 10 min): strength and balance – plank, side plank, Nordic hamstrings, single-leg stance with ball, squats, jumps.
Part 3 (approx. 2 min): running – across the pitch at increasing pace, changes of direction with a clean landing.
With every landing and squat, your knees point over your toes, not inwards.
fifa11.tip: Around 20 minutes before training or a match, two to three times a week. In studies, it markedly reduced the injury rate in youth football (Soligard et al. 2008).
fifa11.caution: After an injury, start with the easiest level and stop if it hurts.
fifa11.progression: Three levels per exercise: easy, medium, hard – only step up once you can do the easier one cleanly.

nordic_hamstring.equipment: partner or fixed foot anchor, mat
steps: Kneel on a soft surface, your heels held down or anchored under a sofa.
Body straight from knees to head, hips extended.
Slowly lower yourself forward, braking with your hamstrings for as long as you can.
Catch yourself with your hands and come back up with a small push.
nordic_hamstring.tip: The best-known exercise against hamstring strains: adding it to prevention programmes roughly halved the rate (van Dyk et al. 2019). Start with 2×4–5 and build up slowly.
nordic_hamstring.caution: Not with a fresh strain. The first few times bring serious muscle soreness – start with few reps, and not on the day before a match.
nordic_hamstring.progression: First lengthen the lowering phase, then add reps (up to 3×8), later go slower.

steps: Side plank on your forearm with your top leg resting on a bench (knee at first, later your foot).
Your bottom leg hangs freely beneath the bench.
Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line – the inside of your top leg carries you.
Hold briefly, lower with control, switch sides.
copenhagen.tip: Strengthens the adductors – the groin is a common injury site in football. 2×6–8 each side.
copenhagen.caution: If you have groin pain, don’t load it – get it checked.
copenhagen.progression: From knee on the bench to foot on the bench (longer lever), then bring your bottom leg up to the bench.

steps: Lie on your side, hips and knees bent at about 45°, feet stacked.
Your pelvis stays upright while your top knee opens like a clamshell.
Keep your feet together.
Slowly close again.
clamshell.tip: Stabilises your pelvis and knees when you run (less “caving in”). 3×15 each side.
clamshell.caution: Don’t roll backwards – the movement comes from your hip.
clamshell.progression: With a mini band above your knees, then hold briefly at the top.

steps: Mini band above your knees or around your ankles, knees slightly bent.
Keep tension on the band as you walk sideways or diagonally forwards.
Knees point forwards, your upper body stays still.
Take the same number of steps in both directions.
monster_walk.tip: A good warm-up before a run or a match. 2–3×10 steps each direction.
monster_walk.caution: Don’t let your knees cave inwards.
monster_walk.progression: Stronger band, or the band around your ankles.

steps: Stand at a step or a wall, knees bent about 30–45°.
Keep your knees bent and raise your heels as high as you can.
Hold briefly at the top.
Lower slowly (3 seconds).
soleus_raise.tip: When you run, the soleus carries several times your body weight – key for your Achilles tendon and calf. 3×15–20.
soleus_raise.caution: If your Achilles tendon is irritated, work slowly and keep pain low.

steps: Ankle drills: short, quick steps on the balls of your feet, 20 m.
High knees: quickly alternate your knees up to about hip height, upper body upright, 20 m.
Heel flicks: heels towards your glutes, quick cadence, 20 m.
Jog back easily in between; finish with 2–3 strides.
running_drills.tip: Improves running economy and coordination – ideal after your warm-up jog before speed sessions. 2 rounds.
running_drills.caution: Only when warmed up, on level ground.
running_drills.progression: Higher cadence, then skipping and bounding.

steps: Feet hip-width apart, knees almost straight.
Small, quick jumps from your ankles only – the floor is “hot”.
Land quietly, keep ground contacts short.
20–30 seconds, then rest.
pogo_jumps.tip: Simple plyometrics: makes your tendons more resilient and your stride springier. 3×20 s.
pogo_jumps.caution: Not with Achilles or shin pain; only after a few weeks of calf strength work.
pogo_jumps.progression: Longer, then single-leg or sideways over a line.

steps: Hold the weight in front of your chest with both hands, elbows pointing down.
Feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned slightly out.
Sink upright into a deep squat, elbows between your knees.
Drive back up through your whole foot.
goblet_squat.tip: The weight in front of your chest keeps your upper body upright – ideal for learning a clean squat. 3×8–12.
goblet_squat.caution: Keep your back straight; with knee pain, only go as deep as is pain-free.
goblet_squat.progression: Heavier weight, then a 2 s pause at the bottom.

steps: Wide stance, toes turned well out.
Hands in front of your chest, upper body upright.
Let your hips sink straight down, pushing your knees out over your toes.
Drive up through your heels and squeeze your glutes at the top.
sumo_squat.tip: Targets your inner thighs and glutes. 3×12–15.
sumo_squat.caution: Your knees follow the direction of your feet – don’t let them cave in.
sumo_squat.progression: With a kettlebell between your legs, then lower more slowly.

steps: Stand tall, hands on your hips or relaxed.
Take a big step backwards with one leg.
Bend both knees; your back knee sinks towards the floor.
Push through your front heel back to standing, switch sides.
reverse_lunge.tip: Easier on the knees than stepping forwards – a good place to start. 3×8–10 each side.
reverse_lunge.caution: Your front knee stays over your foot; if your balance is shaky, hold on to a wall.
reverse_lunge.progression: With dumbbells, then stepping back from a step (deficit).

steps: Wide stance, toes pointing forwards.
Shift your weight to one side and bend that knee, hips back.
Your other leg stays straight, both heels on the floor.
Push back to the centre and switch sides.
side_lunge.tip: Strengthens your legs sideways – important for changes of direction in football. 3×8 each side.
side_lunge.caution: Only go as deep as your heels stay down; your knee points over your foot.
side_lunge.progression: Deeper, then with a weight in front of your chest.

steps: Stand on one leg, knee slightly bent.
Tip your upper body forwards and lift your free leg behind you.
Your back and rear leg form a line, your pelvis stays level.
Slowly come back up, driving through your glutes.
single_leg_deadlift.tip: Strengthens your glutes and balance – very close to running. 3×8 each side.
single_leg_deadlift.caution: Don’t let your pelvis rotate open; with back pain, only go down to horizontal.
single_leg_deadlift.progression: With a dumbbell in the opposite hand.

steps: Rest your shoulder blades against a bench, feet planted hip-width apart.
Raise your pelvis until your knees, hips and shoulders form a line.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top, chin slightly towards your chest.
Lower with control without resting all the way down.
hip_thrust.tip: The most powerful exercise for your glutes. 3×10–12.
hip_thrust.caution: Don’t arch your lower back at the top – the power comes from your glutes.
hip_thrust.progression: Single-leg, then with a weight on your hips.

steps: Lie on your back, one foot planted, the other leg straight in the air.
Raise your pelvis by pushing through your heel.
Your pelvis stays level; hold briefly at the top.
Lower slowly, switch sides.
single_leg_bridge.tip: Quickly shows differences between your sides. 3×10 each side.
single_leg_bridge.caution: Don’t let your pelvis drop to one side; if the back of your thigh cramps, move your foot closer to your glutes.
single_leg_bridge.progression: Hold longer at the top, then with your foot raised.

steps: Stand slightly wider than hip-width, kettlebell in both hands.
Push your hips back and swing the kettlebell back between your legs.
Drive your hips forwards explosively – your arms are just ropes.
The kettlebell floats up to chest height and falls back into the next swing.
kettlebell_swing.tip: Strength and conditioning in one – a staple of Hyrox training. 3×15.
kettlebell_swing.caution: Keep your back straight, don’t pull with your arms; master the hip hinge first.

steps: Half squat, arms back.
Jump up explosively, swinging your arms.
Land softly on the balls of your feet and go straight into the next squat.
Your knees point over your feet as you land.
jump_squat.tip: Explosive power for accelerating and jumping. 3×8–10.
jump_squat.caution: Only with healthy knees, on firm, non-slip ground; land quietly.
jump_squat.progression: More reps, then jumps onto a box.

steps: Feet hip-width apart, hands behind your head.
Bend your knees slightly, push your hips back and tilt your straight upper body forwards.
Go to about horizontal, or until you feel a pull at the back.
Come back up by driving through your hips.
good_morning.tip: Teaches the hip hinge without weight – good preparation for deadlifts. 3×10–12.
good_morning.caution: Your back stays straight, don’t let it round; skip it if you have back pain.
good_morning.progression: With a pole or a light weight on your shoulders.

muscles: shin muscle (front of the lower leg)
steps: Lean your back against a wall, feet about one foot length in front of it.
Your heels stay on the floor; pull your toes up hard towards your shins.
Hold briefly at the top.
Lower slowly.
tibialis_raise.tip: Strengthens the front of your lower leg – helps against shin splints. 3×15–20.
tibialis_raise.caution: With acute shin pain, only work pain-free and get it checked.
tibialis_raise.progression: Feet further from the wall, then single-leg.

steps: Stand on one leg on a step, the other leg hanging in front of the edge.
Slowly bend your knee until the heel of your free leg taps the floor.
Your knee stays over your foot, your pelvis level.
Push back up through the heel of your standing leg.
step_down.tip: Trains knee stability for downhill running. 3×8 each side, slowly (3 s down).
step_down.caution: Don’t let your knee cave inwards; with kneecap pain, use a lower step.
step_down.progression: Higher step, then with a weight in the opposite hand.

steps: Very wide stance, toes turned slightly out.
Shift your weight to one side and sink deep into a squat on that side.
Your other leg stays straight; your toes may point up.
Move through the centre to the other side.
cossack_squat.tip: Hip strength and mobility in one. 3×6 each side.
cossack_squat.caution: Only go as deep as your heel stays down; no jerky movements.
cossack_squat.progression: Deeper, then with a light weight in front of your chest.

steps: Grab two heavy weights at your sides and stand up tall.
Shoulders down and back, abs braced.
Walk with short, steady steps – your upper body doesn’t sway.
30 to 40 metres or 30 seconds, then set them down.
farmers_carry.tip: Grip strength and core stability – a Hyrox station. 3×30 s.
farmers_carry.caution: Pick up and set down the weights with a straight back.
farmers_carry.progression: Heavier, then longer or one-sided (suitcase carry).

steps: Stand about an arm’s length from the wall, ball in front of your chest.
Drop into a deep squat.
Extend explosively and throw the ball to a target high on the wall.
Catch the ball and go straight into the next squat.
wall_ball.tip: Full body and conditioning – a Hyrox station. 3×15.
wall_ball.caution: Back straight, knees over your feet; use a light ball while you learn.
wall_ball.progression: Heavier ball, higher target, more reps.

steps: Dumbbells on your shoulders, feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down, elbows pointing forwards.
Drive up from your legs and press the dumbbells overhead in one movement.
Back to your shoulders and straight into the next squat.
thruster.tip: Transfers power from your legs to your arms – and tests your endurance too. 3×10.
thruster.caution: Don’t arch your lower back overhead; skip it if you have shoulder pain.

steps: Hands slightly wider than shoulder-width on a stable edge.
Your body forms a line from head to toe.
Lower your chest to the edge, elbows angled back.
Push up powerfully.
incline_pushup.tip: The easy way into push-ups – the higher the edge, the easier. 3×10–15.
incline_pushup.caution: The edge must be non-slip; don’t let your hips sag.
incline_pushup.progression: Lower edge, then knee push-ups, then full push-ups.

steps: Knees on the mat, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
A straight line from knees to head.
Lower your chest to the floor with control.
Push up without bending at the hips.
knee_pushup.tip: A stepping stone to full push-ups. 3×8–12.
knee_pushup.caution: Pad your knees; your hips stay in line and aren’t pushed up.
knee_pushup.progression: More reps, then a few full push-ups.

steps: From a push-up position, push your hips up high – an upside-down V.
Hands shoulder-width apart, head between your arms.
Bend your elbows and lower your head towards the floor in front of your hands.
Push back up powerfully.
pike_pushup.caution: Not with shoulder or neck pain; lower slowly.

steps: Hands shoulder-width apart on the edge behind you, fingers pointing forwards.
Legs out in front, your glutes just in front of the edge.
Bend your elbows backwards and lower your body.
Push back up through your arms.
bench_dip.tip: Triceps with your own body weight. 3×8–12.
bench_dip.caution: Go no lower than your upper arms horizontal; skip it if you have shoulder pain.
bench_dip.progression: Straighten your legs further, then feet raised.

steps: Stand tall, dumbbells with your palms facing forwards.
Your elbows stay at your sides.
Curl the dumbbells up to your shoulders.
Slowly straighten your arms again.
biceps_curl.caution: Don’t swing the weight up with your back.
biceps_curl.progression: Heavier dumbbells, then lower more slowly (3 s).

steps: Stand tall, holding one dumbbell overhead with both hands.
Your upper arms stay next to your head.
Lower the dumbbell behind your head.
Straighten your arms again.
triceps_extension.tip: Strengthens the back of your upper arms. 3×10–12.
triceps_extension.caution: Don’t arch your lower back, brace your abs; with shoulder pain, go lighter or skip it.

steps: Stand tall, dumbbells at your sides, elbows slightly bent.
Raise your arms out to the sides up to shoulder height.
Your shoulders stay down – don’t shrug them up.
Lower slowly.
lateral_raise.tip: A light weight is enough – technique is what counts. 3×12–15.
lateral_raise.caution: Not above shoulder height and without momentum; skip it if you have shoulder pain.
lateral_raise.progression: Slightly heavier, then hold for 1 s at the top.

steps: Grip the band shoulder-width apart, arms stretched out in front of your chest.
Pull the band apart until your arms are spread out to the sides.
Shoulder blades together, shoulders down.
Slowly return.
band_pull_apart.tip: Counters a rounded desk posture – works as a quick break too. 3×15.
band_pull_apart.caution: Don’t arch your lower back to compensate, and don’t let the band snap back.
band_pull_apart.progression: Stronger band, then hold for 2 s at the end.

steps: Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width and hang.
Actively pull your shoulders down.
Pull your chest towards the bar until your chin is over it.
Lower yourself slowly.
pullup.tip: At first, use a band for assistance or just practise the slow lowering. 3×3–8.
pullup.caution: No swinging; skip it if you have shoulder pain.
pullup.progression: From slow lowering to your first full pull-up, then more reps.

steps: Lie under a sturdy table or a low bar and grip the edge.
Your heels stay on the floor; your body forms a straight line.
Pull your chest to the edge, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower slowly.
inverted_row.tip: A pulling exercise with no equipment – balances out push-ups. 3×8–12.
inverted_row.caution: Check first that the table or bar will safely take your weight.
inverted_row.progression: Move your feet further forward or raise them.

steps: Place one knee and the hand on the same side on the bench, your back horizontal.
The dumbbell hangs in your free hand.
Pull your elbow close to your body towards your hip.
Lower slowly, then switch sides.
single_arm_row.tip: Back strength with your back safely supported. 3×10 each side.
single_arm_row.caution: Your back stays straight and doesn’t twist open.
single_arm_row.progression: Heavier dumbbell, then a 1 s hold at the top.

steps: Lie on your side, head resting on your lower arm, legs straight.
Lift your top leg, keeping it straight, toes pointing forwards.
Your pelvis doesn’t tip backwards.
Lower slowly, then switch sides.
side_lying_leg_raise.tip: Stabilises your pelvis and knees when you run. 3×15 each side.
side_lying_leg_raise.caution: Only go as high as your pelvis stays still.
side_lying_leg_raise.progression: With a mini band, then a 2 s hold at the top.

steps: On all fours, knees under your hips.
Keep one leg bent and push the heel towards the ceiling.
Don’t arch your lower back; your pelvis stays level.
Return slowly, then switch sides.
donkey_kick.tip: Targets your glutes and is easy on your back. 3×12 each side.
donkey_kick.caution: Only go as high as your back stays straight.
donkey_kick.progression: With a mini band above your knees or an ankle weight.

steps: Lie on your back, hands loosely behind your head, shoulders slightly raised.
Pull one knee to your chest and straighten the other leg.
Rotate the opposite elbow towards the bent knee.
Switch sides smoothly.
bicycle_crunch.tip: Slow works better than fast. 3×10 each side.
bicycle_crunch.caution: Don’t pull on your head; if your back hurts, keep the straight leg higher.
bicycle_crunch.progression: Slower, with the straight leg lower.

steps: Sit tall, knees bent, upper body leaning back slightly.
Hands together in front of your chest.
Rotate your upper body to one side, hands towards the floor beside your hip.
Rotate to the other side, keeping your back long.
russian_twist.tip: Turn from your core, don’t just swing your arms. 3×10 each side.
russian_twist.caution: If your back hurts, keep your feet on the floor and rotate less far.
russian_twist.progression: Lift your feet, then add a weight.

steps: Lie on your back, arms by your sides, knees bent above your hips.
Curl your pelvis up and pull your knees towards your chest.
No momentum; your head stays down.
Lower slowly.
reverse_crunch.tip: Strengthens your lower abs in a back-friendly way. 3×10–12.
reverse_crunch.caution: No swinging; if your neck bothers you, consciously keep your head down.
reverse_crunch.progression: Slower, with a 1 s hold at the top.

steps: High plank, feet slightly wider than hip-width.
One hand taps the opposite shoulder.
Your hips stay still and don’t rock.
Keep alternating.
shoulder_tap.tip: Resists twisting – for a stable core. 3×10 each side.
shoulder_tap.caution: If your wrists bother you, work on your fists or with your hands raised.

steps: On all fours, toes tucked under.
Lift your knees a few centimetres off the floor.
Your back stays flat like a table.
Hold, breathing calmly.
bear_plank.tip: Core tension you’ll feel quickly. 3×20–40 s.
bear_plank.caution: Lift your knees only slightly; don’t round your back.
bear_plank.progression: Hold longer, then move forwards in a bear crawl.

steps: Lie on your back, arms overhead, legs straight.
Lift your arms and legs at the same time – reach your hands towards your feet.
Hold the V briefly at the top.
Lower slowly.
v_up.tip: Demanding – master crunches and leg raises first. 3×8–10.
v_up.caution: Not if you have back pain; no momentum.
v_up.progression: Slower, with a 1 s hold at the top.

steps: Lie on your back, hands beside or under your glutes.
Legs straight, just above the floor.
Small, quick up-and-down kicks, alternating.
Your lower back stays on the floor.
flutter_kicks.tip: Short and clean rather than long with an arched back. 3×20–30 s.
flutter_kicks.caution: If your lower back lifts, hold your legs higher.

steps: Lying on your back, lift your hips into a bridge.
Lift one knee at a time, as if you were marching.
Your pelvis stays up and level.
Lower slowly once you’ve done your reps.
glute_bridge_march.tip: Combines glute strength and pelvic stability. 3×8 each side.
glute_bridge_march.caution: Don’t let your pelvis drop to one side; keep the movement slow.

steps: Deep lunge, both hands on the floor inside your front foot.
Lower your inside elbow towards your front foot.
Then rotate that arm up to the ceiling, your eyes following it.
Come back and switch sides.
worlds_greatest_stretch.tip: Mobilises your hips and back in one go – ideal for warming up. 4–5 each side.
worlds_greatest_stretch.caution: Stay within a pain-free range; lower your back knee if needed.
worlds_greatest_stretch.progression: Take longer breaths in each position.

steps: From all fours, tuck your toes under.
Push your hips up and back – an upside-down V.
Back long, heels sinking towards the floor; your knees may be bent.
Hold, breathing calmly.
downward_dog.tip: Stretches the whole back of your body. 3×30 s.
downward_dog.caution: If your wrists or shoulders bother you, do it on your forearms.
downward_dog.progression: Hold longer, lowering each heel in turn.

steps: Lie on your front, hands beside your shoulders.
Slowly lift your chest; your pelvis stays on the floor.
Shoulders down, eyes forward.
Hold briefly, then lower.
cobra.tip: A gentle extension after long periods of sitting. 6–8 reps.
cobra.caution: Only go as far as feels comfortable in your lower back.
cobra.progression: Hold longer, straighten your arms further.

steps: Stand tall on one leg, holding on to a wall if needed.
Pull the heel of your other leg towards your glutes.
Your knee points down, your hips slightly forward.
Hold, then switch sides.
quad_stretch.tip: The classic after a run. 2×30 s each side.
quad_stretch.caution: Don’t arch your lower back; if your knee bothers you, loop a towel around your foot.
quad_stretch.progression: Hold longer, consciously tucking your pelvis under.

steps: From all fours, bring one knee forwards between your hands, your shin lying across.
Stretch your back leg out long behind you.
Your hips sink towards the floor; upper body upright or folded forwards.
Hold, then switch sides.
pigeon_pose.tip: A deep glute stretch – feels good after long runs. 2×30–45 s each side.
pigeon_pose.caution: If your knee hurts, angle your shin less across or do the figure-four stretch instead.
pigeon_pose.progression: Fold your upper body further forwards, hold longer.

steps: Stand side-on to a wall and hold on.
Swing your outside leg loosely forwards and back.
Your upper body stays still and upright.
Gradually build up the swing, then switch sides.
leg_swings.tip: A dynamic warm-up before running. 10–15 each side.
leg_swings.progression: Bigger range of motion, also sideways across your body.

steps: Stand tall, arms long.
Big, slow circles forwards.
Then change direction.
Your shoulders stay relaxed.
arm_circles.tip: Loosens your shoulders before training. 10 in each direction.
arm_circles.progression: Bigger circles, also one arm at a time.

steps: Half-kneel facing a wall, your front foot about a hand’s width away from it.
Push your knee towards the wall; your heel stays on the floor.
Hold briefly and come back.
Gradually increase the distance, then switch sides.
ankle_rocks.tip: More ankle mobility for deep squats and a smooth running stride. 10 each side.
ankle_rocks.caution: Your heel stays down; if the front of the joint hurts, go less far.
ankle_rocks.progression: Move your foot further away from the wall.

steps: Stand or sit tall, shoulders relaxed.
Tilt one ear towards your shoulder.
Rest the hand on the same side gently on your head – don’t pull.
Hold, then switch sides.
neck_stretch.tip: Relaxing after long periods of sitting. 2×20 s each side.
neck_stretch.caution: Gently does it; if your arms tingle, release straight away.
neck_stretch.progression: Actively push the opposite shoulder down.

steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, one hand on your hip.
Stretch your other arm overhead.
Lean to the side without tipping forwards.
Hold briefly, straighten up, switch sides.
side_bend_stretch.tip: Lengthens your sides – good after sitting. 4 each side.
side_bend_stretch.caution: Don’t arch your lower back; your pelvis stays centred.
side_bend_stretch.progression: Hold longer, reach your arm further over your head.

steps: From standing, bend forwards and put your hands on the floor.
Walk your hands forwards into a push-up position.
Hold briefly, then walk your hands back.
Roll up slowly.
inchworm.caution: Your knees may be bent; not with acute back pain.
inchworm.progression: Add a push-up when you’re in the push-up position.

steps: Stand shoulder-width apart, toes turned out slightly.
Sink into a deep squat, heels staying on the floor.
Your elbows gently press your knees outwards, chest open.
Hold, breathing calmly.
deep_squat_hold.caution: If your knees hurt, go less deep; put something under your heels if needed.
deep_squat_hold.progression: Hold longer, shifting your weight from side to side.

steps: Stand tall, arms by your sides.
Jump your legs apart and raise your arms overhead at the same time.
Jump back to the starting position.
Light and springy, in a steady rhythm.
jumping_jack.caution: On a soft surface; with knee or pelvic floor problems, skip the jump (step to the side).

steps: Run on the spot.
Drive your knees up to hip height, alternating quickly.
Land on the balls of your feet, arms swinging along.
Your upper body stays upright.
high_knees.tip: Short and intense – ideal for intervals. 3×20 s.
high_knees.caution: Only when you’re warmed up and on a non-slip floor.

steps: Run on the spot.
Bring your heels towards your glutes, alternating.
Short, quick ground contacts.
Upper body upright, arms swinging loosely.
butt_kicks.tip: Running drills on the spot. 3×20 s.
butt_kicks.caution: Only when you’re warmed up and on a non-slip floor.

steps: From standing, drop into a squat, hands on the floor.
Jump your feet back into a push-up position.
Jump your feet back in.
Jump up with your arms overhead and land softly.
burpee.tip: Full-body conditioning – part of Hyrox training. 3×8–10.
burpee.caution: Learn it without the jump first (step your feet back); keep your back straight in the push-up position.
burpee.progression: With a push-up on the floor, then a burpee broad jump.

steps: High plank, hands under your shoulders.
Pull one knee to your chest.
Switch legs quickly, alternating.
Your hips stay low and still.
mountain_climber.tip: Core and cardio in one. 3×20–30 s.
mountain_climber.caution: If your wrists bother you, do it with your hands raised on a bench.

steps: Stand on one leg, slightly bent.
Jump sideways onto the other leg.
Land softly, your free leg swinging behind your standing leg.
Keep going back and forth in rhythm.
skater_jump.tip: Lateral jumping power and stability – good for football. 3×20–30 s.
skater_jump.caution: When you land, your knee points over your foot, not inwards.
skater_jump.progression: Jump further, hold briefly on landing.

steps: Bear plank: your knees hover just above the floor.
Move the opposite hand and foot forwards a short way.
Your back stays flat, your hips still.
Crawl forwards and back.
bear_crawl.tip: Coordination and core strength – kids enjoy it too. 3×20–30 s.
bear_crawl.caution: Small steps, knees just above the floor.
